name: Hip thrust
cue: Tuck your chin and drive through your heels until your hips lock.
research: research.json biomech.hip_thrust: upper back on the rounded front edge of a low bench (edge top 0.37 m above the footplate), feet flat, hip pad across the lower abdomen; trunk -50 -> -90, hip 80 -> 0, knee 117 -> 90, ankle -13 -> 0, abduction 10. Spine neutral (lumbar and thorax flex 0): the pelvis and ribcage move as one unit, so the lockout is pure hip extension with the torso level and shins vertical, never a lumbar arch. Machine: the pad carriage is pinned to two levers that pivot on towers in front of the feet (research moving_path: a shallow arc about a pivot in front of the feet); lever 1.06 m, hub 0.91 m high. The pelvis position follows back-plane tangency to the edge; the back contact height is set by the researched angles at A and B (c 0.747 / 0.760, mid-scapula) and solved at 5 via keys so the lever pin stays on the lever circle (length constant to 1 mm): the back rolls about 4 cm over the edge mid-rep, and the hips rise 0.29 m on a nearly vertical path. Levers and pins run in the planes x +-0.27 H, outboard of the fists and forearms. Hands hold handles on the carriage: the research grip beside the hips (elbow 20) puts the fists and forearms over the lateral glutes from the side camera, so arm angles are not targeted. Edge height: with this rig's proportions the researched angles put the bench edge at 0.37 m (research 0.40-0.46 m). The hip pad is a thick roll (0.076 H, 13.5 cm) across the hip crease, so from the low head-side camera it reads as a pad lying on the hips rather than a thin bar floating above the belly; it clears the folded thighs at the stretch and presses 3 mm into the lower abdomen at lockout. Geometry: tools/design/hip_thrust.mjs. Load: plate horns on the levers 0.14 H in front of the tower hubs (the levers are hinged on the hubs; their angle is keyed from the pad-end position, so the plates rise with the hips). (tools/design/loads.mjs)

camera.note: Research view az 95 / el 5. Turned 24 deg further toward the head end and lowered 10 deg (az 119, el -5: 29 deg off the true profile, camera just below hip height, floor plate edge-on): at lockout the glutes face the floor, and the low view from the head side shows them as the underside of the raised hips; it also foreshortens the lying figure so it fills more of a portrait stage. The levers run from the hips to the towers in front of the feet, above the thighs, clear of the torso and glutes.

skinChecks.note: upper back stays on the bench edge
